QF.id: Cat III AIF Due Diligence and Risk_7

question.text: Counterparty Risk for a Cat III AIF can arise from:

answer.text: Brokers, dealers, banks, NBFCs, distributors, custodians and other financial institutions until transactions settle

explanation.text: The Logic: Counterparty risk arises from financial institutions the fund transacts with — brokers, dealers, banks, NBFCs, distributors, custodians and other financial institutions — until transactions settle. CDS counterparties and derivative/debt-market infrastructure are also relevant counterparty exposures. The Trap: Narrow lists framed around only equity exposure, expenses or trustee issues miss the financial-institution counterparties at the heart of the workbook definition. Note: Evaluate counterparty concentration across brokers, dealers, banks, NBFCs, custodians and other intermediaries the AIF actually deals with.
